files.processing: Radiance .hdr decoded (run-length RGBE) and its RGBE bytes written unchanged as an 8-bit RGBA PNG (asset-hdr-to-rgbe-png.mjs, PNG filter type 1 on every row, zlib level 9); no resize, no tone change.
files.notes: Equirectangular interior (a warm bar at night), RGBE bytes in an RGBA PNG: linear RGB = (R, G, B) * 2^(A - 128) / 255; row 0 is the zenith. Alpha is data: decode before any filtering, never through a 2D canvas. Every row uses PNG filter type 1 (see asset-hdr-to-rgbe-png.mjs).

files.colorSpace: RGB: irradiance through the sRGB curve; A: linear
files.processing: Light map of the club room's shell: for each texel of the shell's second UV set, the irradiance of every fixed emitter with soft shadows (CPU ray casting against the shell, the props, the luminaire and both tables), bounced light and an occlusion-weighted ambient, and in alpha the visible share of the main lamp. RGB = irradiance / 16 through the sRGB curve with a 4 x 4 ordered dither; 1024 x 1024 RGBA8 PNG, adaptive row filters, zlib level 6, the bake's record in a tEXt chunk. The same light on a 28 x 8 x 24 grid over the room (six receiver directions per grid point, the same encoding) rides in a private ancillary chunk (rlVo, 129024 bytes before zlib): the furniture reads it. Deterministic: the same tree gives the same bytes.

files.notes: No third-party input: geometry, emitters and albedo hints all come from the code listed under inputs. At run time the room refuses the file when its signature (shell layout, light-map charts, emitter ids and positions, the props plan) does not equal the live room, then the analytic light is used. The exact test is the tool's: `node web/tools/club/bake-room.mjs check` rebuilds the room from the tree and compares content hashes of every blocker triangle, the emitter table and the albedo hints with the record in the file; re-bake when it reports a difference.

files.processing: The arena hall as seen from one point (0, 1.2 m over the floor, 0): six 90-degree views of the hall under its baked light map (no balls, no cue, no haze; the table as a matt stand-in), rendered linear without tone mapping at four times the face's size and averaged into faces of 128 px in the GL cube convention. 6 levels, each the cube through a cosine-power lobe for a roughness (0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1), stacked top to bottom in one 768 x 252 RGBA8 PNG, six faces a row; RGBE (rgb x 2^(A - 136), scene-linear radiance); adaptive row filters, zlib level 6, the record in a tEXt chunk. No cube is rendered at run time.
